primary_diagnosis_treated: Advanced diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 5) with hypertension, dyslipidaemia, anemia, and type 2 diabetes
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate by 1.25 mg every 2‑4 weeks to target 5‑10 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and reduce proteinuria in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE inhibitor for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients as a cardiovascular risk equivalent

medications.dose: 30 µg subcutaneously weekly (≈0.45 µg/kg for a 70 kg adult)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10‑11 g/dL, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA for CKD anemia when Hb <10 g/dL after iron repletion

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily; may increase to 10 mg if needed
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; add if BP >130/80 mmHg after ACE‑I titration
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends antihypertensive regimen to achieve BP <130/80 mmHg in proteinuric CKD

medications.dose: Start glargine 10 U subcutaneously nightly; aspart 4 U with each main meal; titrate by 1‑2 U to achieve fasting glucose 4‑7 mmol/L and post‑prandial <10 mmol/L
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes with eGFR <30 (metformin contraindicated)
medications.nice_justification: NICE diabetes guideline (NG28) recommends insulin when eGFR <30; aligns with CKD management in NG203

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10.9 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
CKD stage 5 – NSAIDs accelerate progression and cause fluid retention
Both drugs increase risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; patient already planned for ACE inhibitor
eGFR 10.9 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the minimum 20 mL/min/1.73 m² required for use per NICE TA775
Nephrotoxic and contraindicated in advanced CKD

assumptions_warnings: Serum potassium not provided – assume ≤5.0 mmol/L; will check 1‑2 weeks after starting ramipril
Liver function tests not provided – assume acceptable; baseline ALT/AST required before atorvastatin
Calcium, phosphate, PTH, bicarbonate not provided – active vitamin D and phosphate binders withheld until results available
Weight not provided – ESA dose calculated for 70 kg adult; will adjust after actual weight known
Allergy status not provided – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or ESA allergies before prescribing
Blood pressure reading not provided – assume above target; amlodipine added only if needed
treatment_summary: Start ramipril and atorvastatin as first‑line CKD therapies, add darbepoetin alfa for anemia, and initiate basal‑bolus insulin for diabetes (metformin contraindicated). Provide conditional amlodipine for additional BP control. Avoid NSAIDs, metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, and ACE‑I/ARB combination. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, lipids, hemoglobin, and glucose per NG203 recommendations and adjust therapy accordingly.
